div.head: III Atr 13.3
div.ab: Et ubi tainus habet duas optiones. amicitie uel lage, et amicitiam eliget, stet hoc ita firmum sicut ipsum iudicium.
⁊ þar þegen áge twegen costas, lufe oððe lage, ⁊ he þonne lufe geceose, stande þæt swa fæst swa sé dom.
⁊ þar þegen áge twegen costas, lufe oððe lage, ⁊ he þonne lufe geceose, stande þæt swa fæst swa sé dom.
And where a thegn has two alternatives before him—amicable agreement or legal proceedings—and he decides upon the former, it shall be as binding as a legal decision.
And where a thegn has a choice of two things, amicable settlement or legal process, and he then chooses settlement, that is to be as binding as a legal sentence.
Und wo ein Thegn zwei Möglichkeiten [sein Recht vom Gegner zu erlangen] hat, Sühnevertrag oder Rechtsgang, und er nun den Sühnevertrag wählt, so stehe das so fest wie das Gerichtsurtheil.
And where a thegn has two choices [of obtaining his right from his opponent], settlement by agreement or legal process, and he then chooses settlement, let that stand as firm as the judgment.
